pr_body:
macOS 10.7 and 10.8 had a bit wired clang which is detected as `__GNUC__` which has `__ATOMIC_ACQ_REL` but it excepts one option at `__atomic_add_fetch` instead of 2.

This prevents OpenSSL to be compiled on such systems.

Fixes: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18055
pr_comments: @catap note that you either need to submit a completed OpenSSL CLA or, if you think this submission is trivial (and the OpenSSL reviewers agree), you can put "CLA: trivial" in the commit message separated by an empty line from the rest of the message. see https://www.openssl.org/policies/cla.html
@tom-cosgrove-arm I've already sent signed CLA
Just made a force push with reworded comment. This comment should make clear also point which was raised by @paulidale
In light of the comments in #18055, do we still want this "fix"?

@paulidale it fails without MacPorts on clean system => this fix is required from my point of view.

[Here](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18055#issuecomment-1091852198) Ken confirmed that on his system it also failed without macports stuff.
Cool thanks.  It wasn't completely clear, looking again I misread something somewhere.

> Cool thanks. It wasn't completely clear, looking again I misread something somewhere.

yeah, it isn't because discussion was across a few different places:
 - here
 - https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18055
 - https://trac.macports.org/ticket/64947
 - https://github.com/macports/macports-ports/pull/14498
 
 So, missread and miss some context was quite easy :)

@paulidale it is definite that early versions of clang's `__atomic_add_fetch()` are incompatible with the current form of this function, so avoiding `__atomic_add_fetch()` on those versions is absolutely correct

What's not certain is if just the first argument could be used, but for such old versions of both clang and OS/X it seems that known correctness - and possibly slightly slower execution (falling back to locks) - would trump "faster, but unknown if it's not broken in other, subtle, ways"

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.
@AenBleidd did this PR help you at any way? Otherwise I suggest to close it.
@catap I'll check it during next 24 hours and let you know. Thank you for notifying me
@AenBleidd it is broken on clang until version 3.1 https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/01ba47d7b6c0dfabb9014e6d904b71e55f0428ed but I not sure that such version is used anywhere.
So this should not be merged yet?

@catap, ok, I checked this and this patch (mostly lines 203, 230 and 255) is essential for me.
Even on NDK 21d and ANDROID_API 30 I was not able to build for Android x86 without this patch (the error was still the same).
So if you consider not to add changes for particular versions of clang for OSX, at least keep the lines I mentioned above with `BROKEN_CLANG_ATOMICS` macro verification.
Thanks a lot!
P.S. If you consider not to support these broken clang compilers - that would be still fine because I can create a custom patch (that I should then support but anyway) and go on with it. But this patch would be really nice to have.
@AenBleidd I feel that we should understand which version of compiler have you used. Can you share output of `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null | grep clang` for your toolchain?

@catap 
```
./i686-linux-android16-clang -dM -E -xc /dev/null | grep clang
#define __clang__ 1
#define __clang_major__ 9
#define __clang_minor__ 0

#define __clang_version__ "9.0.8 (https://android.googlesource.com/toolchain/llvm-project 98c855489587874b2a325e7a516b99d838599c6f)"
```
@AenBleidd this is wired, it should be ok since clang 3.1 :(
@catap, looks like not in case of Android x86 :(

Do you think PR #16584 is solving for the same issue in a different way?

It fixed my ios armv7 (32bit) build issue and it sounds the same, but uses a different workaround.  More discussion in Issue #16551
@bradh352 this PR is used as part of MacPorts OpenSSL. But it address a bit different issue but on the same pice of code :)
Any updates on this?
@AenBleidd I haven't got access to such toolchain to ping point the differences :(

Is it possible at least to keep a workaround and just remove this block https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/18056/files#diff-33114a13bd417cbc08f1be5b6ba0ae94f1a86516e0635d508d6e7fc55908a423R20-R31 ?

@AenBleidd are you sure that:
```
#if defined(__apple_build_version__) && __apple_build_version__ < 6000000
```
works for you? May you show
```
clang -dM -E -xc /dev/null | grep apple
```
on your clang?

@AenBleidd yep, special in the case that all Apple related mess is related to some old (and not the last) version of toolchain.

If you have an idea why it fails on android x86 and which condition it should satisfied => I'm willing to update this PR :)
I'm not sure about the special condition in this case, so I'd just keep this macro to let user disable these atomics in case of build failure

@catap PR #16584 definitely resolves the android x86 build failure (freebsd i386 and ios armv7 too).  I wouldn't be surprised if it doesn't happen to resolve this issue too since all are clang related.

This PR is to fix a definite issue in older clang where `__atomic_is_lock_free()` was implemented differently to the current/modern/usual implementation in both clang and gcc. Since it changes to a workable (if less performant) alternative on older clang (and only on older clang), I don't see why this PR can't be merged. It fixes a real problem (admittedly with an old compiler) in a way that doesn't impact modern toolchains.
Merged to master and 3.0 branches. Thank you for your contribution.
It also nicely provides a workaround for other environments with broken atomics and clang with `-DBROKEN_CLANG_ATOMICS` on `Configure` command line.

#  ifdef BROKEN_CLANG_ATOMICS
